subject: zoology
question_text: Distinguish between white matter and grey matter of the central nervous system.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.52, VSAQ 88). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: White matter
steps.why: The colour of each region names what is inside it, so the answer works from the colour to the contents.
common_mistakes: Writing that white matter holds the cell bodies. It holds myelinated fibres.
Saying the colour comes from Nissl granules. Those give grey matter its colour.
steps.memory_tip: White means myelin. Grey means cell bodies and Nissl granules.
lines: White matter looks white because of myelin.
It is made of myelinated nerve fibres, that is,

steps.label: Grey matter
steps.why: Myelin is a fatty white sheath and Nissl granules are grey, so the two colours simply report which part of the neuron lies in that region.
common_mistakes: Putting dendrites in the white matter. Dendrites are part of the grey matter.
steps.memory_tip: Grey matter is where the cells live; white matter is where their wires run.
steps.margin_note: One boxed contrast line, then grey matter's own contents.

lines.text: White = myelinated fibres · Grey = cell bodies

lines: Grey matter looks grey because of the Nissl
It is made of cell bodies (cytons), dendrites

insider_note: Two colours, two causes, two contents — write it as a table if there is room, because the examiner is ticking pairs.
